name: fluent-kit
description: Fluent 2 implementation kit: everything needed to build the Fluent UI v9 components on any renderer. All facts derive from Fluent UI React v9 at one commit of microsoft/fluentui and the @fluentui/tokens package it publishes.
readOrder: foundations.json: system rules every spec assumes (token tiers and themes, the state-per-token rule, colour families and pairing, the type ramp and the Selawik stand-in, shape, spacing, the shadow ramp, focus, disabled, motion, high contrast).
tokens/fluent.resolved.json: every token value per theme, keyed by tokens.<name> as Fluent code spells it. Look up any path a spec names here.

components/<id>.json: one spec per component. Build from its tokenGroups plus its layout, states and behaviour rules; its values carry the sizes Fluent hard-codes; read its notes before trusting a token.

conventions.tokenPaths: Strings matching ^(tokens|typographyStyles)\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$ are token paths in tokens/fluent.resolved.json; every one in this kit is checked to exist.
conventions.sources: source fields cite Fluent UI React files as use<Name>Styles.styles.ts:lines or <Name>.types.ts:lines under source/components, the focus helpers under source/focus, or fluent2:<page> for the design site.
conventions.units: px for dimensions, ms for durations; shadows are layers of {x, y, blur, color}; there are no per-corner radii and no springs.

files.describes: The same tokens with alias references, for theming tools.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: A vertical stack of headers that each show or hide a panel of content, for long pages whose sections a reader scans and opens one or a few at a time. Use tabs when sections are peers viewed one at a time, and a tree when items nest or need arrow-key navigation.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A picture of a person or entity: their image, else their initials, else a person icon, on a coloured disc or square, with an optional presence badge and an active ring or shadow. Use it wherever a person is named in a list, header or card; size it to the line it sits beside, and use colorful to tell many initials apart.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Several people as one unit: avatars overlapped in a stack, spread in a row, or cut into a pie, with the overflow behind a button that opens a popover list. Use it for a set of participants; a single Avatar is one person and a Persona a person with text.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A small non-interactive label that draws attention to a status, count or category. Use Badge for short text or an icon with a colour meaning, CounterBadge for a number or unread dot on another element, and PresenceBadge for a person's availability on an avatar.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: A horizontal trail of links from the top of a hierarchy to the current page, so a user sees where they are and can jump up any number of levels. Use a nav for moving between peers and a tab list for views of one thing.

components.name: Button
components.summary: A single-action control. Choose emphasis by appearance (primary > secondary > outline > subtle > transparent), size by the density of the surrounding layout, and shape to match its neighbours; one button per primary action on a surface.

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A month grid for picking a date, with a month picker and a year picker reached through the header, a go-to-today button and optional week numbers. Use it inline where a date is the main content; use date-picker when the date belongs in a form field and the calendar should pop up.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface that groups the content and actions about one subject: a header (image, title, description, action), an optional full-bleed preview and a footer of actions. Choose filled for a raised card on a page, filled-alternative on a Background 1 page, outline where shadows would crowd, subtle for a borderless tile; make it interactive or selectable only when the whole card is one target.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: A horizontal strip of cards shown one group at a time, moved by previous and next buttons, dot navigation, drag or autoplay. Use it for a small set of peer items the user browses in order; use tabs when the sections have names and a list when all should be visible.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: An independent on/off choice, or a parent choice whose children are partly selected (mixed). Choose it over a switch when the change takes effect on submit rather than at once, and over a radio group when any number of options may be chosen.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: A colour chooser assembled from a saturation-and-value area, a hue slider and an alpha slider that share one HSV colour. Choose it for any colour; choose SwatchPicker for a fixed set.

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: A field that opens a listbox of options: Combobox is a text input the user can type into (filtering, or freeform values), Dropdown a button that only picks from the list. Both share the Listbox, Option and OptionGroup parts and one look. Choose Select for a native single pick with no custom option content, a TagPicker for many picks shown as tags.

components.name: CompoundButton
components.summary: A tall button with a large icon, a label and a line of secondary text describing the action, for choices that need a sentence of explanation, such as the options on a start page. Use a plain button when the label says enough.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: A form field for one date: an Input showing the formatted date with a calendar icon, and a Calendar that pops up under it. Use it where a date belongs in a form; use calendar alone where the grid is the content, and time-picker for a time.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A window over the page that asks for a decision or holds a short focused task, with a title, content and a row of actions. Use modal to block the page until it is dismissed, alert when the user must choose an action, non-modal to let the page stay usable; use a drawer for long or side-anchored work.

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A thin horizontal or vertical line separating groups of content, optionally with a short label set into it. Choose emphasis by appearance (strong > default > subtle; brand for accent); prefer spacing alone where it separates clearly enough.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A panel anchored to the start, end or bottom edge of the screen or of a region, holding secondary content or navigation: an overlay drawer floats over the page behind a backdrop and is dismissed, an inline drawer takes its space in the layout beside the content. Use a dialog for a decision that blocks the page.

components.name: Field
components.summary: The wrapper that gives one form control its label, hint and validation message and wires their ids onto the control. Use it around every Input, Textarea, Checkbox group, RadioGroup or Switch that needs a visible label or a message; it draws nothing of its own.

components.name: Image
components.summary: A bitmap in a box: an img element with a shape, an optional border and shadow, and a fit rule for how the source fills the box. Use it for pictures and logos; an Avatar draws a person, a Skeleton a placeholder.

components.name: InfoLabel
components.summary: A Label followed by a small information button that opens a popover of explanatory text. Use it on a field whose name needs a sentence of help; use a tooltip when the help is one short line and a link when it leads elsewhere.

components.name: Input
components.summary: A single-line text entry control with optional content (usually an icon) before and after the text. Choose it over Textarea for one line of text; wrap it in a Field for its label, hint and validation message.

components.name: Label
components.summary: Text that names a form control, with an optional required indicator. Use it through Field where there is one; use it alone only to label a control Field cannot wrap.

components.name: Link
components.summary: Text that navigates, or acts like a button while reading as text. Choose it over a subtle or transparent Button when the action sits inside or beside running text; inline marks one inside a sentence, where it is always underlined.

components.name: List
components.summary: A vertical list of items that can be navigated with arrow keys and, optionally, selected one or many at a time, each item carrying a checkbox when selectable. Use it for rows of like content; a Tree nests, a Menu is for actions, a Table for columns.

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A floating list of commands or options opened from a trigger, for actions that do not warrant a visible button each. Items can carry an icon, a shortcut, a submenu, a checkmark (checkbox or radio) or a switch; use a select or combobox instead when the user picks a value for a form field.

components.name: MenuButton
components.summary: A button that opens a menu, marked by a trailing chevron and styled as selected while its menu is open. Use it as a Menu's trigger when the button does nothing but open the menu; use a split button when there is also a default action.

components.name: MessageBar
components.summary: A persistent, inline status strip the page owns: an intent icon, a bold title running into body text, and actions, laid out on one line while it fits and reflowing to two when it does not. Use it for a condition the user should know about while on the page; use a toast for a passing notification and a dialog for a decision.

components.name: Nav
components.summary: The app's side navigation: a column of items and collapsible categories of sub-items in a drawer, with section headers, dividers, an app title row and a hamburger to open or close it. Use a tab list for views of one page and a breadcrumb for a trail.

components.name: Persona
components.summary: A person: an Avatar or a presence badge beside up to four lines of text, the name first. Use it in lists, headers and pickers; an Avatar alone is the picture without the text.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A floating surface anchored to a trigger, holding any content up to and including buttons and inputs, opened by click and closed by a click outside or Escape. Use it where a tooltip is too small or non-interactive; use a menu for a list of commands, a dialog for something modal, and a teaching popover for onboarding.

components.name: ProgressBar
components.summary: A thin horizontal bar showing how much of a task is done (determinate) or that work is under way with no known end (indeterminate). Choose it over a spinner when the task has measurable progress or runs long enough to warrant a bar in the layout.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.summary: A set of mutually exclusive options, of which exactly one is chosen, each a Radio inside a RadioGroup. Choose it over a dropdown when there are few options (roughly five or fewer) worth showing at once, and over checkboxes when only one may be picked.

components.name: Rating
components.summary: A row of stars that collects a rating (Rating) or shows one with its value and count (RatingDisplay). Choose Rating for input, RatingDisplay for a read-only score, and its compact form for a single star with the number beside it.

components.name: SearchBox
components.summary: An Input specialised for search: a leading search icon, a dismiss control that appears while focused with text, and Escape to clear. It reuses Input's appearances, sizes and states; choose it over a plain Input wherever the value is a query.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A styled native select: one value picked from a platform-drawn list, wearing Input's appearances and sizes. Choose it when the options are plain strings and the platform's own popup is acceptable; choose Combobox or Dropdown for custom option content, multiselect or typing.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A loading placeholder: a group of stencil-coloured shapes in the layout the content will take, shimmering or pulsing until it arrives. Use it where content loads in place; a Spinner is for an action without a known shape and a ProgressBar for a measured wait.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: Picks one number from a continuous or stepped range by dragging a thumb along a rail. Choose it when the relative position matters more than the exact value (volume, brightness); use a spin button or input when the user must type an exact number.

components.name: SpinButton
components.summary: A numeric field with stacked increment and decrement buttons at its end, stepping the value by step (Page keys by stepPage) within min and max and rounding to a precision. Choose it over Input for numbers that are nudged more than typed; choose Slider when the range matters more than the exact value.

components.name: Spinner
components.summary: An indeterminate loading indicator: a ring with a growing and shrinking arc that spins. Choose it over a progress bar when the wait is short or its length unknown and there is no measurable progress, or when the space is too small for a bar.

components.name: SplitButton
components.summary: Two joined buttons: a primary action and a menu button that opens related alternatives. Use it when one action is the usual choice but others belong beside it, as in Save with Save as; use a menu button when there is no default action.

components.name: SwatchPicker
components.summary: A row or grid of swatches, colour, image or empty, of which one is selected. Choose it for picking among a fixed set of colours or textures; choose ColorPicker for any colour.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: A binary on/off toggle whose change takes effect at once, like a physical switch. Choose it over a checkbox when there is no submit step, and over a toggle button when the setting has a persistent on/off meaning rather than an action.

components.name: TabList
components.summary: A row or column of tabs that switches between views of one surface, marking the selected tab with a brand indicator bar (transparent, subtle) or a filled pill (subtle-circular, filled-circular). Choose it over a segmented set of toggle buttons when each option is a whole view, and keep the appearance, size and orientation on the list, never per tab.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Rows and columns of data: a header row of sortable cells over body rows of cells, with an optional selection cell per row, cell layouts for media and two-line content, hover actions and column resize handles. Table is the presentational set; DataGrid composes the same parts over column definitions with sorting, selection, resizing and cell or row focus built in. Use a List for one column of like items.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A compact label for an item the user has picked or that categorises content: text with an optional icon or avatar, a secondary line, and a dismiss icon. Tag is one static or dismissible unit; InteractionTag splits into a primary action button and a secondary dismiss button; TagGroup lays several out with a shared size and dismiss handling. Use a Badge for a status the user does not act on.

components.name: TagPicker
components.summary: A multi-select combobox whose selections show as dismissible tags inside the field: a control holding a tag group, an input to type into and an expand icon, and a list of options in a popover. Choose it over a multiselect Combobox when the chosen items need to stay visible and removable in place.

components.name: TeachingPopover
components.summary: A popover for onboarding and feature callouts: a header line, a title, a body with optional media, and a footer of one or two buttons, or a carousel of such pages with dot navigation. Use it to teach a feature at the point it appears; use a plain popover for ordinary content and a dialog for a decision.

components.name: Text
components.summary: Inline typography: one run of text at a size on the base ramp, in a weight and family, optionally block, italic, underlined, struck through, aligned or truncated. Use it, or its named presets (Body1, Caption1, Title1 and the rest of the ramp), wherever a component does not already set the type; a Label is for naming a control, a Link for navigation.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A multi-line text entry control, optionally resizable. Choose it over Input when the answer may run to more than one line; wrap it in a Field for its label, hint and validation message.

components.name: TimePicker
components.summary: A form field for one time of day: a Combobox listing times at a fixed increment between a start and an end hour, optionally typed freeform. Use it beside date-picker for a time; use combobox itself for any other list.

components.name: Toast
components.summary: A transient notification dispatched into a fixed corner of the screen by a Toaster, with a title, optional body and footer actions, that dismisses itself after a timeout. Use it for the outcome of an action the user did not have to wait for; use a message bar for a persistent status the page owns, and a dialog for anything that needs a decision.

components.name: ToggleButton
components.summary: A button that stays pressed: it flips a single on/off setting, such as bold in a toolbar, and shows the on state with its Selected colours. Use a switch for a setting that takes effect like a form field, and a checkbox inside forms.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A single tab stop holding a row (or column) of related commands: buttons, toggle buttons, radio buttons, groups and dividers. Choose it over loose buttons when several commands act on the same object and should be reached with arrow keys; the items are Button and ToggleButton, so build those first.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short, non-interactive text bubble that labels or describes the element it is attached to, shown on hover and keyboard focus after a delay. Use it for an icon-only button's name or a one-line hint; use a popover for anything interactive or longer than a sentence.

components.name: Tree
components.summary: A hierarchy of items that expand and collapse, navigated with arrow keys and optionally selectable with checkboxes or radios: Tree nests subtrees in the markup, FlatTree takes a flat list with parent values and is the choice for large or virtualised data. Use a nav for app navigation and a list for a flat set.
